Triggers.value: A specific temperature on the skin

Threat.value: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
I scan for exits as soon as I enter any room or building
I notice potential weapons or dangerous objects in any environment

Memory.value: My memories of the frightening event are very clear and detailed.
The memory feels like it is happening right now rather than something that is over
The memory forces its way into my mind when I do not want it to

Negative Appraisals.value: I feel dirty or contaminated because of what happened
The world is a dangerous place
My body has been permanently damaged by what happened

vignette: Señor Juan Vargas, a 67-year-old widowed Latin American prosecutor, sought help after a traumatic sexual assault. The event occurred one evening when he was walking home from his office. As he passed by an unfamiliar alleyway, a stranger grabbed him and forced him into a dark corner, where the assault took place. This incident left Juan with a profound sense of vulnerability and contamination. In the weeks following the assault, Juan's memories became vivid and uncontrolled. The event replayed in his mind as though it were happening again, making it nearly impossible for him to distinguish between past and present. He would often find himself in the middle of a heated courtroom argument, only to be suddenly transported back to that dark alleyway. This intrusive nature of the memory caused significant distress, particularly when he was around children or people related to his late wife. Juan had come to believe that his body was permanently damaged, and the feeling of contamination lingered heavily on him. He avoided touching others and felt a strong aversion to being in close proximity to anyone who reminded him of the attacker. This avoidance extended to physical sensations; even a specific temperature on his skin could trigger intense anxiety and memories of the assault. Juan's occupation as a prosecutor placed him in various settings, each fraught with potential triggers. He would scan for exits the moment he entered any room or building, constantly assessing potential dangers. In courtrooms, he noticed every object that could be used as a weapon, his eyes darting from one corner to another. This hyper-vigilance made it challenging for him to fully engage in his work, and over time, this behavior began to affect his relationships with colleagues. His home life was also impacted. He avoided social gatherings and visits from family members, especially those involving children. The mere presence of a child could provoke intense fear and anxiety. His sense that the world was dangerous made it difficult for him to leave familiar surroundings. As a result, he increasingly stayed indoors, isolating himself from the community he once actively engaged with. What frightened Juan most was the prospect of being assaulted again, and this fear was grounded in his belief that his body was physically vulnerable. He had stopped going to unfamiliar places because he felt unable to assess potential dangers. This avoidance extended even to routine tasks such as grocery shopping or attending social events. Juan's current state is marked by a profound sense of isolation and distress. His work performance has declined, and he feels increasingly disconnected from the world around him. The incident that finally brought him to seek help was an intense panic attack in the courthouse lobby, triggered by a child who looked similar to those he had known. This episode left Juan feeling overwhelmed and realized that without intervention, his quality of life would continue to deteriorate. In therapy, Juan is most hoping for relief from the overwhelming sense of contamination and constant threat. He hopes to regain a sense of safety in public spaces and reconnect with the community he once felt at ease within. His primary fear is the recurrence of the assault and the lasting physical vulnerability it left him feeling. With support, Juan aims to reclaim his life and find peace amidst the lingering trauma.
